archetype: Five-colour Dragon critical-mass deck with a certified combo exit. deck-audit runs it on the combo budget from strategic_frame.json — 4-8 tutors, 4-6 protection — and the deck sits inside both at 7 and 6. The frame's decklist_sha256_prefix is edc6644d0683, which matches cards.json, so it describes this exact 99 and I agree with its reading: 22 of the 24 creature entries are Dragons feeding per-Dragon triggers, and the loop is an exit rather than the spine.
verdict: Four checker-passed stacks certify three independent kills, and two of them — stack 001's Dragon Tempest burst and stack 004's Blasphemous Act redirect — never touch Aggravated Assault, so the deck is not one enchantment away from having no way to win. What limits it is mana at the point of deployment: 34 land copies against 36-38, and a land drop that holds at 88.3% on turn three and then falls to 60.3% on five and 49.7% on six, against 27 entries in the 99 that cost five or more. Card advantage is the second-order cause and reads 4 against a floor of 10, but the uncounted draw in this deck is board-dependent, so it pays on the turns the deck is already winning rather than the turns it is stuck.

axes.reading: Two under the 36-38 band, and the goldfish says where it bites: the turn-3 land drop holds at 88.3% and then falls to 60.3% on turn five and 49.7% on turn six. Those are the turns this deck has to start deploying the 27 entries in the 99 that cost five or more.

cut_candidates.why: Mana value 8, and nothing in the deck discounts it. Of the ten entries at mana value seven or more — Ancient Gold Dragon, Cavern-Hoard Dragon, Drakuseth, Klauth, Old Gnawbone, Tiamat, Utvara Hellkite, Blasphemous Act, Dracogenesis and the commander — eight are Dragon creature spells that Urza's Incubator, Herald's Horn and Dragonspeaker Shaman all reduce (eminence reduces every one of those but the commander itself, which the two artifacts still do), and Blasphemous Act reduces itself. Dracogenesis is an Enchantment with no Dragon type, so it is reached by none of them, in a deck whose mean available mana is 4.937 on turn six and 6.539 on turn ten.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: Dracogenesis casts every Dragon left in hand for free, unlimited per turn, and keeps them. Four other free-deployment effects sit in the 99 and each is narrower: Sneak Attack is repeatable but costs {R} an activation and sacrifices the creature at the next end step; Breaching Dragonstorm and Hellkite Courser are one-shot enters-the-battlefield triggers; Rishkar's Expertise is a sorcery capped at mana value 5. The commander belongs in this price and iteration 1 left it out: The Ur-Dragon reads "Whenever one or more Dragons you control attack, draw that many cards, then you may put a permanent card from your hand onto the battlefield" — repeatable, free, and it does not sacrifice what it deploys. Its conditions are one permanent per combat, put onto the battlefield rather than cast, and Dragons attacking, which needs the nine-mana commander resolved: the goldfish, which models no cost reduction, puts its mean cast turn at 8.967 with 0% by turn six, a floor rather than a schedule. So the cut costs the multi-Dragon turn, not the deploy function. I re-examined the difficulty against that and it stays painful — a free hand of Dragons in one turn is a real ceiling and I am recommending the cut anyway. It is not the deck's highest ceiling: bracket_report lists three two-card infinites, all three name Aggravated Assault, and stacks 003 and 006 certify two of them ending the game.

open_questions.question: At 36 lands (Mana Confluence and Ancient Tomb in, Patriarch's Bidding and Klauth out), do the turn-five and turn-six land-drop rates move off 0.603 and 0.497?
open_questions.why_it_matters: mana-base is the axis I am calling binding, and the prescription is sized on the assumption that two lands move those two numbers. If they barely move, the answer is a lower curve rather than more lands.

open_questions.question: goldfish_targets.json declares no component for either of the two non-Assault kills the checker certified — nothing names Ancient Gold Dragon (stack 001) or Wrathful Red Dragon (stack 004).
open_questions.why_it_matters: The simulation therefore never measures how the median game actually ends. validate-goldfish-targets passes anyway, and its reason sharpens the question. It runs a shape gate plus two substantive checks: declared cards must still be in the 99, and — the one built for exactly this omission — a card appearing in TWO OR MORE checker-passed stacks while belonging to no component is reported as a possible undeclared win line. Ancient Gold Dragon appears in stack 001 only and Wrathful Red Dragon in stack 004 only, so both sit under that quorum of two and the check that would catch them stays silent. Nothing checks that every certified kill is declared.

open_questions.question: Does Old Gnawbone plus Hellkite Charger sustain? The combo record prices the activation at {5}{R}{R} and the question is whether one connection's Treasures fund the next.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would make the extra-combat effect redundant rather than merely tutorable, which is what the corpus asks of a linear deck; and Hellkite Charger is a Dragon, so eminence, the three reducers, Sarkhan's Triumph, Worldly Tutor and Tiamat all reach it.

open_questions.question: Cavern-Hoard Dragon plus Aggravated Assault is listed by bracket_report as a two-card infinite that says 'Target opponent loses the game', and it has no stack artifact.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is one of the three lines forcing the bracket floor to 4, and it is the only one of the three the checker has not seen.

gaps: There is no deck_recon.json for this deck (deck-audit reports recon.present false), so nothing here is grounded in what strong Ur-Dragon lists actually run. Every add comes from the deck's own Short List, which is a pool fact, not a meta fact.

The goldfish explicitly does not model cost reducers, rituals or extra draw, so the commander's mean cast turn of 8.967 and 0% by turn six are a floor and not a schedule — and the deck runs three reducers plus eminence. Nothing in the repo measures the real number.

bracket_report.json carries no decklist_sha256 (deck-audit's freshness block reports current: null for it), so its currency cannot be checked mechanically. I re-ran bracket.assess against cards.json and it returns floor 4 with the same three Game Changers and the same three two-card infinites.

interaction-breadth cannot see Chaos Warp, which removes any permanent at the price of a random replacement, because card_roles.json has no entry for it; six of the 99 have no role at all (Aggravated Assault, Chaos Warp, Dracogenesis, Patriarch's Bidding, Rishkar's Expertise, Sneak Attack). The axis is a floor and I have read the cards behind it, but a role entry for Chaos Warp would settle it mechanically.

Whether Ruby Medallion or Sarkhan, Soul Aflame is the better fourth reducer is not settled by any artifact here: the Medallion is cheaper ({2} against {1}{U}{R}) and reaches more of the deck (mana_analysis puts a red pip on 32 cards), while Sarkhan discounts Dragon spells and so covers the four Dragons the Medallion misses (Ancient Gold Dragon, Dragonlord Dromoka, Old Gnawbone, Korlessa, Scale Singer) and is a 2/4 body that survives Dragonback Assault's 3 damage. I picked on mana cost because mana is what binds.

findings.note: The exception list is now complete and exact. I re-enumerated every Dragon creature entry in cards.json independently: 22 entries (21 in the 99 plus The Ur-Dragon), and exactly four carry no red pip, with the costs quoted verbatim correct — Ancient Gold Dragon {5}{W}{W}, Dragonlord Dromoka {4}{G}{W}, Old Gnawbone {5}{G}{G}, Korlessa, Scale Singer {G}{U}. Both consequences hold. (a) Old Gnawbone is one of exactly THREE mana Dragons: goldfish_targets.json's loop target declares any_of [Old Gnawbone, Savage Ventmaw, Cavern-Hoard Dragon], and deck-audit's engine reproduces it as the size-3 'fodder' component — the number three is the deck's own declaration, not the doctor's estimate. (b) Ancient Gold Dragon is the trigger source in stack 001's scenario block (checker.verdict == pass); the d20 trigger on the stack is its own. Supporting figures re-derived: mana_analysis R.cards is 32 and I recomputed it from cards.json pips independently (32, commander included), Ruby Medallion is {2} 'Red spells you cast cost {1} less to cast' and is a colourless artifact so identity-legal in WUBRG, and it sits in deck-audit's own closers.by_role for this component (ramp:cost-reduction, edhrec 300). 'Thinnest declared component' is the audit's per-target field, not a free superlative: the size-3 reducer component carries thin=true and thinnest=true in deck-audit's engine block. Two residual imprecisions I checked and am not opening as findings: Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm is also a Dragon on stack 001's board, so 'the Dragon in stack 001' is loose — but Ancient Gold Dragon is the stack's subject and the point (this is not a marginal card) survives; and the mana-dragon group ties the reducer group at 3 while Aggravated Assault is thinner at 1, which the same document's engine block states outright ('the thinnest component in the deck by a factor of three'), so no reader is misled.

The re-scoped clause is true of all six, checked card by card against oracle_text in cards.json, and the six are exactly the removal:damage carriers in card_roles.json (Blasphemous Act, Boros Charm, Dragon Tempest, Dragonback Assault, Drakuseth, Scourge of Valkas). Dragon Tempest 'Whenever a Dragon you control enters, it deals X damage to any target' and Scourge of Valkas 'Whenever this creature or another Dragon you control enters...' are ETB-gated; Drakuseth is attack-gated; Dragonback Assault's ETB is '3 damage to each creature and each planeswalker' and Blasphemous Act is '13 damage to each creature', both symmetric; Boros Charm's damage mode is 'target player or planeswalker' and none of its three modes removes a creature. So none of the six is a targeted creature answer on demand — the claim holds. The double count is disclosed AND accurate: Boros Charm is in deck-audit's protection axis card list (protection:self) as well as the interaction list, and the reading says so in the same sentence.
